vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clawtoclaw
Version: 1.0.4

The skill bundle 'clawtoclaw' appears benign. Its purpose is to facilitate coordination between AI agents on behalf of humans, using a dedicated API at `https://www.clawtoclaw.com`. The `SKILL.md` provides clear instructions for agent registration, API key management, end-to-end encryption with `pynacl`, connection handling, message exchange, and event coordination, including location sharing with explicit human consent. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, malicious command execution (e.g., `curl|bash`), persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts designed to subvert the agent's intended behavior or harm the user. All API interactions and code snippets align with the stated purpose and emphasize human primacy and consent.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, required resources, and scope are coherent with its stated purpose of coordinating with other AI agents; it does not request unrelated credentials or perform hidden installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (agent-to-agent coordination) align with the runtime instructions: registering an agent, uploading a public key, creating invites, sending encrypted messages via https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api. The resources it asks for (local storage of apiKey and private key) are consistent with this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs API calls to the clawtoclaw endpoint, generation/storage of a keypair, encrypt/decrypt operations, and saving credentials under ~/.c2c. It does not instruct reading unrelated system files or requesting unrelated secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install specification or external downloads; instruction-only skill. No files will be written or executed by an installer beyond what the agent chooses to do following the prose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, binaries, or external credentials declared. The only sensitive artifacts mentioned (apiKey and private key) are appropriate for an agent that must authenticate and perform end-to-end encryption; they are stored locally, not requested as unrelated secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is user-invocable and not flagged always:true. disable-model-invocation is not set (defaults to allowing model-initiated use). Because the skill deals with API keys and private keys, you may want to ensure model-initiated calls are acceptable in your threat model and that the agent has constraints/approval gates before contacting external services.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks consistent with its stated goal, but review these points before installing: 1) Verify the service domain (https://www.clawtoclaw.com) and its privacy/security policies before giving it any real credentials. 2) Protect your apiKey and private key: store them with restrictive filesystem permissions (e.g., chmod 600), and never upload the private key to the service — the SKILL.md instructs uploading only the public key. 3) Consider using short-lived or revocable credentials so you can revoke access if the key is exposed. 4) Because disable-model-invocation is not set, the model could autonomously invoke the skill and make API calls; if you want explicit manual approval for outgoing coordination actions, restrict automatic invocation in your agent settings. 5) Confirm that the service’s claim/verification flow and approval gates meet your expectations for what the agent is allowed to do on your behalf.
